NON-SYCOPHANTIC-CONVERGENCE ARTIFACTS PRESERVED IN FULL ON STACK 2026-05-23. The seven verbatim cross-model artifacts (which previously existed only inside the cross-model chat transcripts, not on disk) are now saved on the stack at ~/.sovereign/non-sycophantic-convergence/: ARTIFACTS_README.md, prompt_source_tokens_v3.md, chronicle_failure_profile_v2.md, prompt_source_tokens_loader.py, prompt_source_tokens_ddl.sql, chronicle_failure_profile_loader.py, chronicle_failure_profile_ddl.sql. SHA-256 manifest written to SHA256SUMS.txt in that directory (re-verify any time with: shasum -c SHA256SUMS.txt). A verify/ subdir holds the Tier 2 harness (verify_chronicle_loader.py) and its captured output (output.txt). The as-received original is retained at ~/Downloads/claude-work-5-23-26-files/. PROVENANCE CHAIN: Gemini 3.5 Flash -> Anthony as human relay -> web-chat Claude extraction -> zip -> HQ-Opus. The chain is asserted, not independently proven; the integrity check named in the README is whether these files match Anthony's Gemini conversation history.

TIER 2 VERIFICATION BY EXECUTION (the verbatim chronicle_failure_profile_loader.py was imported and run, never edited on disk; the one missing name was injected at runtime only to reach the later lines): BUG 1 (missing import unicodedata) CONFIRMED as a hard runtime NameError, NOT "probably implicit" as the README hedged - Python has no implicit import, so the function always crashes at the normalization line. BUG 2 (noop encode/decode roundtrip) CONFIRMED a noop across the test battery; ADDED FINDING - the roundtrip raises UnicodeEncodeError on a lone surrogate (U+D800), so it is not perfectly inert, and the recommended fix (drop the roundtrip, call unicodedata.normalize directly) also removes that latent crash path. BUG 3 (NFC ordered last vs the spec's NFC-first) CONFIRMED as a real spec-vs-code divergence but BEHAVIORALLY INERT for NFC: 0 of 6 crafted cases (combining marks, em spaces, CRLF, blank lines, space+combining) produced any difference. NFC has no canonical decomposition that adds or removes whitespace, so it commutes with strip/split/CRLF normalization. The README's stated rationale ("NFC can produce character-width changes that affect whitespace") is actually an NFKC property, not NFC. The reproducibility risk bug 3 poses is therefore SMALLER than the design exchange implied; this corrects the handoff's framing.

FINDINGS BEYOND THE THREE NAMED BUGS: FINDING A (arguably more material than bug 3) - the line " ".join(text.split()) collapses ALL whitespace including newlines into single spaces, so (i) the subsequent .replace CRLF->LF is dead code, and (ii) the code does NOT implement the spec's line handling: both vector records say collapse vertical line breaks to a single LF (preserve newlines), but the code destroys newline structure entirely. This changes the signature hash. FINDING B - the loader SELECTs from a chronicle_ledger table (doc_id, raw_text, log_timestamp) whose schema is NOT in chronicle_failure_profile_ddl.sql; the DDL only defines chronicle_failure_profiles_v2 and alters vector_admission_registry (parent schema also unprovided). The ledger table had to be invented to run the loader. Undocumented dependency. FINDING C (observed by reading, NOT executed) - the spec mandates ISO-8601 timestamps with a Z UTC offset, which datetime.fromisoformat parses to tz-AWARE datetimes on Python 3.11+; the loader compares them with t_start <= log_time <= t_end, which raises TypeError if any compared timestamp is tz-naive. Latent, data-dependent; the harness used naive timestamps deliberately to isolate the three named bugs. DB DIALECT MISMATCH (README-noted) CONFIRMED - function types db_conn as sqlite3.Connection while the DDL is PostgreSQL (UUID/JSONB/TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE/gen_random_uuid()); schema had to be adapted to SQLite to run.

RUN-2 reproducible signature_hash over the synthetic 3-document manifest: 32ff6ff0960279d09dd5e2b1830f57fac6369378471c37938478bb01dbed7f4d (evidence the function works once the import is fixed).

METHODOLOGY NOTE (candidate THIRD data point for the format-divergence finding, held as evidence-not-proof per ChatGPT's guardrail): executing the concrete artifact surfaced divergences (newline destruction, bug-3 inertness, undocumented ledger table) that conceptual review and the chronicle summaries had not. Consistent with the prior finding that concrete-artifact pressure exposes what continued conceptual refinement misses. Single artifact, single model family - not generalized.
